##### \[English below]

Це питання вирішується у **Так**, якщо між **5 травня 2025** року та **1 липня 2025** року з'являться достовірні повідомлення про те, що Збройні сили України (ЗСУ) мають щонайменше одну крилату ракету Taurus KEPD 350 або її модифікацію (детальніше див. у секції Fine Print), або про те, що ЗСУ здійснили запуск такої ракети.

Альтернативно, воно вирішеться у **Так,** якщо ракета однозначно вказана на [сторінці, присвяченій військовій підтримці України](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/news/military-support-ukraine-2054992), на офіційному веб-сайті Федерального уряду Німеччини. Якщо ця сторінка буде недоступною, джерелом для вирішення питання може бути інша сторінка того ж офіційного сайту, за умови, що вона містить перелік військової техніки, поставленої Німеччиною в Україну.

Якщо жоден з цих критеріїв не буде виконаний до **1 липня 2025** року, питання вирішується як «Ні».

***

This question resolves as **Yes** if, after **May 5, 2025** and before **July 1, 2025**, there are credible reports that the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) possess at least one Taurus KEPD 350 cruise missile or its variant (see the Fine Print for details), or that the AFU have launched one.

Alternatively, the question will resolve as **Yes** if the missile is unambiguously listed on the [page dedicated to military support for Ukraine](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/news/military-support-ukraine-2054992) on the German Federal Government’s official website. If this page becomes unavailable, another page from the same official website may be used as a resolution source, provided it includes a list of military equipment delivered to Ukraine by Germany.

If none of these criteria are met by **July 1, 2025**, the question resolves as **No**.

question: Will a large language model (LLM) solve ≥ 40% of FrontierMath questions before May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve **"Yes"** if, by **May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET**, a **AI lab announces that one of their  LLMs** (which can include a LLM using tools like Python) successfully solves at least **40% of the questions** on EpochAI's **FrontierMath** benchmark. The whole system must submit only one answer to each question. This rules out things like pass@n (mark correct if any of the n trials were correct) but consensus@n is allowed (most likely answer on n trials) since this can be implemented by only submitting one answer.

#### **Evaluation Criteria:**

* The **primary resolution source** will be any announcement by a **major and credible** AI lab including but not limited to **OpenAI, DeepMind, Meta, Anthropic**, **X, and Deepseek.**
* If multiple reports exist, the **most credible and widely accepted evaluation** (e.g., from **OpenAI, DeepMind, Meta, Anthropic, or academic researchers**) will be used.
* If an LLM **achieves ≥40% accuracy** on **the set** **of FrontierMath problems** before the deadline, the question will resolve **"Yes."**
* If no LLM achieves this threshold by **May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET**, the question will resolve **"No."**

question: By May 15, 2025, will there be a frontier reasoning model that is publicly and unambiguously known to conduct much of its reasoning via a medium other than natural language?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve **"Yes"** if, by **May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET**, there is **public and unambiguous evidence** that a **frontier AI reasoning model** from any of the following labs:

* **XAI**
* **Meta**
* **Deepseek**
* **Anthropic**
* **DeepMind**
* **OpenAI**

is conducting **much of its reasoning** through a medium that is **not natural language**. This could include, but is not limited to:

1. **Neuralese** – The model uses an **internal vector-space representation** for thinking, which is significantly different from human-readable natural language.
2. **Extreme Linguistic Drift** – The model's reasoning chains use **tokens that resemble words but are largely meaningless to humans** and follow a non-natural language structure.

#### **Evidence Requirements for "Yes" Resolution**

It must be a **frontier model**. This means that the company markets the model as being better than their previous offerings. This is in contrast to a research output like [https://github.com/facebookresearch/coconut](https://github.com/facebookresearch/coconut).

At least one of the following must be **publicly confirmed** by **the model's developer** or through **credible AI research publications**:

* **A paper, official blog post, or technical report** from one of the listed AI labs explicitly states that the model **relies on non-natural language reasoning.**
* **Open-source model weights or logs** show clear evidence of reasoning in a **vector space or another non-linguistic medium.**
* **Public statements from senior researchers at these organizations** (e.g., interviews, conference talks) explicitly confirm the model’s reasoning mechanism as **not primarily based on natural language.**

#### **Resolution Conditions for "No"**

This question will resolve **"No"** if, by May 15, 2025:

* No public evidence confirms that a **frontier reasoning model** conducts reasoning outside natural language.
* Research suggests AI still predominantly uses **natural language chains of thought** with no significant shift toward **neuralese or extreme linguistic drift.**
* Speculative reports or theoretical papers exist but lack concrete **public** evidence of implementation.

question: Will the Russia-Ukraine war end before May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve **"Yes"** if **a clear and verifiable end to the Russia-Ukraine war** is established **before May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET** through one or more of the following:

#### **Primary Resolution Conditions (Any One of These Would Resolve "Yes")**

1. **A Formal Peace Treaty or Ceasefire Agreement:**
   * A **legally binding agreement** is signed between the governments of **Russia and Ukraine** that officially **ends the war** or **establishes a permanent ceasefire.**
   * The agreement must be **publicly confirmed** by at least **two major independent sources**, such as:
     * **The United Nations (UN)**
     * **The U.S. State Department or another major government entity**
     * **The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE)**
     * **Reuters, BBC, Associated Press, or another major news agency**
2. **An Unambiguous, Lasting End to Major Combat Operations:**
   * If **both** of the following are true for at least **one full month (30 days)** before May 15, 2025:
     * No **major military offensives** or significant fighting between Russian and Ukrainian forces.
     * No **active territorial disputes or claims of war by either government.**
   * This must be **confirmed by multiple independent sources** (e.g., **BBC, Reuters, AP, NYT, The Guardian**).
   * A short-term lull or pause in fighting **does not** count—there must be **clear indications of a lasting cessation of hostilities.**
3. **A Major Political Resolution Recognized by Both Governments:**
   * If **Ukraine and Russia both declare publicly that the war has ended** and **cease further military actions**, even without a formal treaty.
   * This declaration must be **officially stated** by **both** the **Russian** and **Ukrainian** governments **and acknowledged by at least two reputable sources.**

### **Primary Sources for Resolution:**

* **International & Governmental Sources**
  * [United Nations](https://www.un.org/)
  * [Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE)](https://www.osce.org/)
  * **Official statements from the governments of Ukraine & Russia**
* **Major News Agencies**
  * [BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/)
  * [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/)
  * [Associated Press (AP)](https://apnews.com/)
  * [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/)

If conflicting reports exist, a **majority consensus from primary sources** will determine resolution.

question: Will OpenAI release an LLM product or API that hallucinates 5x less than GPT-4 did when it was released, by June 30, 2025?

This question resolves as **YES** if, by June 30, 2025, OpenAI releases an LLM product or API that claims it scores >=95% on its internal factual eval, _OR_ >= 92% on TruthfulQA, and **NO** otherwise.

question: Will an AI system solve one of the remaining Millennium Prize Problems before July 2025?
resolution_criteria:
The question resolves **Yes** if, before July 1, 2025, a Millennium Prize Problem is solved by an AI.

The question will resolve upon announcement by the Clay Mathematics Institute, or when at least 2 reputable papers (e.g., on arXiv or in peer-reviewed journals) show a correct solution. If the solution is disputed or inconclusive, resolution may be postponed until a consensus is reached.

The question will resolve **Yes** if most of the major elements of the solution were primarily discovered by the AI. The contribution of humans should be limited to:

- Creating the system
- Feeding the system with previously established knowledge
- Stating the problem in a form understandable to the AI
- Converting the solution into a form understandable by humans
- Other tasks unrelated to the core of the solution.

The AI should be understood broadly as any computation system that is not human.

question: Longbets series: will the June, 2025 Labor Force Participation Rate and unemployment rate, reported by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, be, respectively above 60 percent and below 7.5 percent?
resolution_criteria:
Robert D Atkinson and Jason W Galbraith summarize their reasons for taking the bet [here](https://longbets.org/687/).

Robert D Atkinson argued,

> Increasingly a large number of pundits and scholars, including Eric Brynjolfsson, Martin Ford, Andrew McAfee, and Vivek Wadhwa, have argued that technology is rapidly advancing and will soon lead large scale displacement of workers with technology. These views have rapidly become the prevailing wisdom regarding emerging technology with the result being that voters and policy makers are now more likely to resist technological change and automation, rather than embrace it. But the "robots are killing our jobs" proponents miss the fact that automation lowers prices (or raises wages) which in turn spurs increased demand for goods and services, and hence labor. As such there is no reason to believe that either unemployment or the share of adults in the workforce will decline in any significantly way going forward.

Alberto Forchielli countered,

> The United States will certainly experience a recession in the next six years. As a result, the workforce participation rate will fall below 60 percent and this time, automation and de-industrialization will keep it there at least through June 2025.

***Will the June, 2025 Labor Force Participation Rate and unemployment rate, reported by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, be, respectively above 60 percent and below 7.5 percent??***

If Robert D Atkinson is declared the winner of the bet by the Long Now Foundation, then this question resolves positively. If Jason W Galbraith is declared the winner, then this question resolves negatively.
